chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman al-Asam, from Mis'mam ibn al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"If a slave performed Hajj ten times, one Hajj would still be obligatory upon him as the Hajj of Islam, if he had the means to do so. And if a boy performed Hajj for ten years, then upon reaching puberty, the obligatory Hajj of Islam would be due upon him. And if a slave performed Hajj ten times, then was freed, the obligatory Hajj of Islam would be due upon him if he had the means to do so."

key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: The obligatory Hajj (the first one required of a Muslim)
key_terms.فَرِيضَةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: The obligatory duty of Islam (referring to Hajj)

ai.seo_question: Does performing Hajj multiple times as a slave or child exempt one from the obligatory Hajj later?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle that voluntary or preparatory Hajj performances do not discharge the primary obligation (*Hajjat al-Islam*) until the specific conditions of maturity, freedom, and financial capacity are met. It establishes a clear legal distinction between *nafl* (voluntary) acts performed during periods of non-obligation and the *fard* (obligatory) duty that becomes due upon the onset of these conditions, ensuring the integrity of the religious duty is preserved regardless of prior piety.
